newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGE opens up, Havas falls.
newsitem.headline: CGE opens up, Havas falls.

text.p: Shares in Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) opened 2.18 percent higher at 750 francs on Friday, while shares in media group Havas opened down 1.71 percent at 441.30 francs.

Both shares had been suspended on Thursday, pending their announcement late in the day that CGE would become the majority shareholder of Havas with 30 percent, and Havas would become the majority shareholder in Canal Plus with a 34.4 percent as part of a restructuring of their media activities.
CGE said it would sell Havas its 19.3 percent stake in pay-television company Canal Plus for 5.6 billion francs and its Generale d'Images unit for 526 million.
It will obtain a stake of some 30 percent in Havas through the issue of new shares in exchange for the assets and by buying eight million Havas shares for 3.4 billion francs from Alcatel Alsthom.
Chairman Jean-Marie Messier said the deal with Havas would boost his company's earnings per share by 10 percent in 1997.
Havas said its share capital will rise from 12 to 14 billion francs due to the capital increase to give CGE a higher stake.
Havas said it expected to show a net attributable profit ahead of write-downs for goodwill of just over 1.2 billion francs in 1996, compared with 1.11 billion in 1995.
As trade continued, Havas shares fell further, trading down 2.43 percent at 438.10 francs. CGE shares were up 3.81 percent at 762 francs at 0930 GMT.
"It's a very good deal for Generale des Eaux," a trader said. "And as for Havas, I think some sellers may regret it because we may be in for good surprises from them in terms of asset sales."
